title: Preserve egress resolver binding across peering handoffs to prevent cross-tenant hostname exposure
creator: Marisol Reyes
description: Customer escalation: production Dedicated tenants intermittently observe private hostnames resolving to other tenant services after GPU pool reassignments or peering switchover events. Root cause analysis shows a timing window where egress resolver bindings (UDP/TCP sockets and conntrack entries) are reused across ephemeral SNAT mappings during peering/route handoffs. When a peering session tears down and re-establishes, existing conntrack entries and resolver sockets can be re-associated to a different tenant VNI before name-resolution state (cache, in-flight queries) is reconciled, allowing stale responses or external-resolver fallback to surface private hostnames across tenants. This ticket implements a production fix that preserves tenant boundary on resolver binding and hardens handoff behavior during pool/peering changes. The approach: 1) Tag conntrack/egress-socket state with the tenant-id and peering-session-id; 2) Refuse reuse of resolver sockets/conntrack entries if tenant-id mismatch; 3) Ensure deterministic ordering in peering teardown: mark egress sockets stale and drain pending queries before allowing new tenant reuse; 4) Add a short TTL-based probe/flush window after peering handoffs to avoid stale cache re-association; 5) Add telemetry and alerting for any resolver socket reuse event and post-handoff DNS mismatch rate. The fix must be performant (no per-request synchronous calls to control-plane) and compatible with Dedicated autoscaling and fast GPU pool handoffs. Backwards compatibility: older conntrack entries will be evicted using a conservative flush strategy to avoid mass outage. A canary rollout with 5% of customers in Dedicated and explicit customer opt-in for high-risk tenants is planned. Documentation and postmortem will be produced for on-call and support teams.
updates: 2026-03-10: Triage call with oncall+SRE+Networking. Customer provided PCAP and resolver logs from Dedicated region eu-west-1.
2026-03-11: RCA complete - identified conntrack reuse + SNAT rotation race as primary vector. Drafted design: add tenant_id + peering_session_id tags to egress-state and policy to reject reuse.
2026-03-12: Prototype implemented in lab: tagging works and blocks cross-tenant reuse; end-to-end latency overhead ~0.3ms median on egress path. Added unit tests for tag logic.

2026-03-13: Integration test with autoscaler choreography and peering failover simulated. Observed rare 1/100k query drops during synchronous drain; implemented soft drain + retry to eliminate visible customer impact.

2026-03-14: Security review kick-off scheduled. Preparing rollout plan: canary 5% (non-critical tenants) -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks. Drafted customer notification for impacted accounts and support playbook.
Next steps: finalize code PR, complete security review, create infra migration job to tag active state, schedule canary, monitor resolver_reuse_alert metric and customer DNS mismatch rate.
verification_steps: Deploy to dev cluster with synthetic tenants and repeated peering toggles
Run chaos test: simulated peering teardown/bringup while running high-QPS DNS load
Validate no cross-tenant A/AAAA/CNAME exposure in packet captures
communication_notes: Customer-facing: short description of root cause, expected timeline for fix, recommended mitigations (e.g., pinning critical tenants to Dedicated reserved pools until fix is rolled out)
